statement.summary: Lemma A.2 is frozen as three Props for real q ≥ 2: `lemA2Part1Statement` ([d j]_q ≤ 4q^{j(d−j)}), `lemA2Part2Statement` ([d 1]_q ≤ 2q^{d−1}) and `lemA2Part3Statement` (Σ_{j=2}^d r_d(q,j) ≤ 4(d−1)q^D); `lemA2Statement` is their conjunction. The Gaussian binomial is the product formula `gaussProd` over ℝ, as the lemma says, not the q-Pascal `gaussBinom`. The sharper ℕ-estimate `gaussBinom_le_pow` ([d r]_q ≤ 2^d q^{r(d−r)}, Lemmas/Ineq.lean) belongs to the core proof of Theorem 6.1 and does not certify this lemma.
deltas: [d j]_q is `gaussProd q d j = ∏_{i<j} (q^{d−i} − 1)/(q^{i+1} − 1)` over ℝ (ℕ-subtraction d − i exact for i < j ≤ d).
r_d(q,j) is `rdReal q d j = q^{C(j,2)} · gaussProd q d j`.
Unstated ranges made explicit: d ≥ 1 (standing) and, in (1), j ≤ d, so j(d−j) is exact ℕ-subtraction. (For j > d the product formula is 0, so the restriction loses nothing.)
Σ_{j=2}^d is Σ over `Finset.Icc 2 d` (empty for d = 1); 4(d−1) uses real subtraction; D = `DD d = d(d−1)/2` (exact ℕ-division).

maps.label: three estimates

tex.text:
Let $q\ge2$ be real, with $\gaussbinom dj_q$ and
$r_d(q,j)=q^{\binom j2}\gaussbinom dj_q$ defined by the product formula.
Then $\gaussbinom dj_q\le 4q^{\,j(d-j)}$,
$\gaussbinom d1_q\le 2q^{\,d-1}$, and
$\sum_{j=2}^{d}r_d(q,j)\le 4(d-1)\,q^{D}$

maps.note: The hypothesis, the definitions and the three estimates; the estimates are frozen separately and conjoined.

maps.label: q ≥ 2 real
maps.note: q is a real number in all three parts.

maps.label: d ≥ 1 (standing), j ≤ d (implicit)
maps.note: The lemma states no range for d and j. Lean takes the standing d ≥ 1 (Definition 2.1), which (3) needs: at d = 0 its right side 4(d−1)q^D = −4 is negative while the empty sum is 0. In (1) it adds j ≤ d, which loses nothing: for j > d the product formula contains the factor q^{d−d} − 1 = 0, so [d j]_q = 0.

maps.label: [d j]_q by the product formula
maps.note: The §3 product formula with p replaced by the real q.

maps.label: 'defined by the product formula'

lean.text: noncomputable def gaussProd (q : ℝ) (d r : ℕ) : ℝ

maps.note: For non-integer q the q-Pascal `gaussBinom` (ℕ-valued) is unavailable, hence a separate ℝ definition. Applying the lemma to integer q needs the bridge `gaussBinomEqProdStatement`.

lean.text: gaussProd q d j ≤ 4 * q ^ (j * (d - j))

maps.label: 4q^{j(d−j)}
maps.note: Natural-number exponent; d − j exact as j ≤ d.

maps.label: 2q^{d−1}
maps.note: d − 1 is ℕ-subtraction, exact under d ≥ 1.

lean.text: ∑ j ∈ Finset.Icc 2 d, rdReal q d j ≤ 4 * ((d : ℝ) - 1) * q ^ DD d

maps.label: Σ_{j=2}^d r_d(q,j)

lean.text: ∑ j ∈ Finset.Icc 2 d, rdReal q d j

maps.note: Sum over the interval [2, d] (empty for d = 1).

maps.label: D := d(d−1)/2
maps.note: ℕ-division, exact since d(d−1) is even (`DD_eq_choose`: DD d = C(d,2)).
